concerns.text: Task T012a [P] implements `src/data_ingestion/verify_data.py` and claims to depend on T043/T044, but T043 and T044 are listed *after* T012a. This creates a consumer‑before‑producer dependency violating the data‑flow ordering.
Unit test T010 is scheduled before the implementation task T013 (`src/data_ingestion/loader.py`). Tests must consume the artifact produced by the loader, so the test should come *after* T013.
Integration test T011 is placed before the graph‑construction and threshold tasks (T014, T015, T016). The test depends on a constructed graph, so it must be ordered after those producer tasks.

Contract test T012 validates serialized graphs against `graph.schema.yaml` but is scheduled before the serializer task T016, which actually produces the JSON files. This is a consumer‑before‑producer ordering error.

Task T005b is marked `[P]` yet writes to the same `src/constants/material_lattice.yaml` file created by T005. Because they share mutable state, they cannot safely run in parallel; the `[P]` tag is inaccurate.

Task T012a is marked `[P]` but writes to `state/data_status.json`, a shared state file that is also read/modified by several other tasks (T012b, T012c). Parallel execution could cause race conditions; the `[P]` tag should be removed or the task should be sequenced.
